Abstract: The transition from the Internet of Things (IoT) to the Internet of Agents (IoA) necessitates a fundamental paradigm shift in physical layer security, moving from static, rule-based defenses toward autonomous, agentic resilience. However, current embodied nodes often lack the cognitive capability required to handle adaptive, intelligent threats. We propose employing Generative AI (GAI) as the cognitive engine—rather than merely a signal processing tool—to empower agents to construct an internal world model of the physical environment. In this work, we present a holistic agentic security framework that instills autonomy across two key dimensions. First, Endogenous Self-Evolution allows agents to utilize GAI for predictive environmental modeling and autonomous resource decision-making, thereby self-calibrating against hardware impairments. Second, Exogenous Active Defense implements a generative observe-orient-decide-act (OODA) loop. This loop enables agents to autonomously execute intelligent threat perception, confrontation planning, and a strategic duality of behavioral concealment and identity camouflage. Finally, we discuss the path toward general-purpose security agents via neuro-symbolic architectures. This survey bridges the gap between signal generation and agentic reasoning, defining a new era where security becomes an innate, evolving property of collaborative embodied intelligence.

Abstract: Residential construction projects are characterized by high complexity, fragmented communication, and vulnerability to delays and budget overruns due to inefficient manual coordination. A multi-phase evaluation with 11 medium and large construction enterprises demonstrated the system's capability to reduce coordination latency, improve schedule adherence, and eliminate dependence on costly cloud application programming interface (APIs). This paper proposes a Zero Trust-based security architecture for Agentic AI using Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs) and a Policy Decision Point (PDP). It also defines PDP decision attributes such as subject identity, source trustworthiness, code and tool integrity, requested privilege, data sensitivity, task context, andruntime state. By mapping Agentic AI risks to concrete PEP/PDP controls, this paper provides a structured architecture for preserving agent autonomy while limiting unsafe actions, contaminated context propagation, and unauthorized externalinteractions.

Abstract: In order to make industrial robotic arms adaptively accomplish the uniform grinding tasks for tubular workpieces of different sizes, spatial orientations and surface characteristics, a parameterized planning framework is proposed in this paper. Compared to the state-of-the-art methods and algorithms, performance advantages of the planning framework proposed are at least 16.94%, 21.60%, 28.78%, 4.59% and 48.68% in terms of size estimation, spatial orientation estimation, convergence rate, solution quality and computational complexity respectively. Therefore, in this paper, a new planning method is suggested to not only generate grinding paths for both tee tubes and elbows but also make all grinding experience accumulated till now used in new grinding tasks by combining deep reinforcement learning and the heuristic optimization algorithm. Abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is an AI paradigm that can perceive the environment, reason over observations, and execute actions to achieve specific goals. Task-oriented communication supports agentic AI by transmitting only the task-related information instead of full raw data in order to reduce the bandwidth requirement. In real-world scenarios, AI agents often need to perform a sequence of actions to complete complex tasks. Completing these long-horizon tasks requires a hierarchical agentic AI architecture, where a high-level planner module decomposes a task into subtasks, and a low-level actor module executes each subtask sequentially. Since each subtask has a distinct goal, the existing task-oriented communication schemes are not designed to handle different goals for different subtasks. To address this challenge, in this paper, we develop a hierarchical task-oriented communication (HiTOC) framework. We consider a system with an edge server and a robot as an edge device. The high-level planner and low-level actor modules reside on the edge server. The robot transmits only the environmental observation that is relevant to the current subtask to the edge server. We propose a conditional variational information bottleneck (cVIB) approach to train the HiTOC framework to adaptively transmit minimal information required for each subtask. Simulations conducted on the AI2-THOR platform demonstrate that the proposed HiTOC framework outperforms three state-of-the-art schemes in terms of the success rate on MAP-THOR benchmark.

Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) and imitation learning (IL) have made great progress in robotic decision-making in recent years. However, these methods show obvious deterioration for new tasks that need to be completed through new combinations of actions. RL methods suffer from reward functions and distribution shifts, while IL methods are limited by expert demonstrations which do not cover new tasks. In contrast, humans can easily complete these tasks with the fragmented knowledge learned from task-agnostic experience. Inspired by this observation, this article proposes a task-agnostic learning method (TAL for short) that can learn fragmented knowledge only from task-agnostic data to accomplish new tasks. TAL consists of four stages. First, the task-agnostic exploration is performed to collect data from interactions with the environment. The collected data is organized via a knowledge graph. Second, an action feature extractor is proposed and trained using the collected knowledge graph data for task-agnostic fragmented knowledge learning. Third, a candidate action generator is designed, which applies the action feature extractor on a new task to generate multiple candidate action sets. Finally, an action proposal network is designed to produce the probabilities for actions in a new task according to the environmental information. The probabilities are then used to generate order information for selecting actions to be executed from multiple candidate action sets to form the plan. Experiments on a virtual indoor scene show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art offline RL methods and IL methods by more than 20%.

Abstract: Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are increasingly adopted in industrial logistics due to their flexibility and ability to operate without dedicated infrastructure. This research presents the design and implementation of a LiDAR-based autonomous navigation system for a semi-heavy mobile robot with a payload capacity of 100 kg. The primary objective is to achieve environmental mapping and reliable autonomous navigation in indoor environments without reliance on physical guidance systems or wheel odometry. The proposed system integrates a 2D LiDAR sensor within the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework and employs the Hector SLAM algorithm for real-time map generation and localization. Autonomous navigation is achieved using the ROS Navigation Stack, incorporating global and local planners for path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance. In addition, a custom middleware interface is developed to safely transmit velocity commands from the high-level planner to the low-level motor controller. Experimental evaluations conducted in real-world corridor environments demonstrate robust navigation performance, achieving a positioning error of less than 10 cm, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach for industrial logistics applications.

Abstract: With increasing task complexity in space robotic mission designs, advancement in the command technology and remote operation of the robotic team becomes a key challenge for providing an effective human-robotic team interface to help facilitate successful task execution. In the International Space Station (ISS)-to-ground telerobotic experiments, Surface Avatar led by DLR with partner ESA, a team of robots on the (Earth) surface is commanded by an astronaut in orbit to perform various tasks in a simulated space habitat. The ISS crew can select different input modalities to command the robots with direct teleoperation with the aid of force reflection in some instances, which provides great user immersion and interaction with the environment. At the other end of the Scalable Autonomy spectrum, the robot team can also be commanded at the task level, utilizing the robot's local intelligence to plan and execute at the crew's high-level direction. By scaling and mixing these telerobotic command capabilities, we can bring human and robot intelligence together to solve and execute more complex and unknown tasks. The teleoperator, whether an astronaut or ground-based expert, would be able to effectively command a surface robotic team in a wide variety of conditions. A concern raised for autonomously executed robotic task is the ability to cope with unexpected situations in a timely manner. To help enhance this command scalability, particularly for a more seamless transition between the command modes, the current research presented in this paper introduces a system that allows the crew to intervene with direct user input to provide course correction during autonomous task execution mid-task execution. This work explores different solutions to provide the human teleoperator with situational awareness of the robot's action, and approaches for user intervention. One approach we developed provides guidance forces based on the autonomous task and uses the movement of the haptic device as a comparison metric for interpreting the user intention. The user can observe the robot's action via the video stream, and let the robot complete the task autonomously. The robot executes the tasks autonomously as long as the robot's planned action (e.g. motion) concurs with user's intention. Should the need or desire arise, the user can take over with direct teleoperation at any moment using the haptic interface. The haptic cues provided by the haptic input device can take different forms such as pose, position, or velocity. In order to understand the effectiveness of these different approaches for allowing the teleoperator to take over the robot's autonomous task, particularly for space deployment, an implementation for user intervention is tested during the Surface Avatar ISS-Earth telerobotic experiment in 2025 where the ISS crew commanded a team of robots to perform various sample handling tasks with Scalable Autonomy teleoperation. Its outcome and astronaut feedback are discussed. Furthermore, a user study is carried out on-ground in the same simulated space habitat with the time-delay conditions experienced by the ISS crew to study the performance and usability of seamless switching of telecommand modalities in Scalable Autonomy teleoperation.

Abstract: The proliferation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite mega-constellations presents a compelling opportunity for planetary-scale broadband connectivity, yet simultaneously introduces formidable routing challenges rooted in the continuous evolution of inter-satellite link (ISL) topology at orbital velocities approaching 7.5 km/s. Conventional shortest-path protocols exhibit convergence deficiencies during ISL transition intervals, occasionally precipitating routing loops under dynamic conditions. This paper proposes an adaptive routing framework grounded in deep reinforcement learning, specifically employing Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), to address these shortcomings. A Walker Delta constellation of twelve satellites at 550 km altitude is simulated under physically motivated link constraints—a 5,000 km optical range limit and a strict Earth-occlusion check— within a custom Python-based orbital environment. The routing agent observes a 182-dimensional state vector encoding satellite positions, pairwise distances, link connectivity states, and per-node queue depths. A dynamic action masking layer restricts the agent’s decision space to physically reachable neighbors at each step, substantially accelerating policy convergence. Deployed within a hybrid architecture that invokes Dijkstra’s algorithm as a confidence-gated fallback, the combined system achieves a 100% packet delivery rate across all evaluated scenarios, compared to 94.2% for unassisted hop-count routing. The PPO agent achieves a standalone routing efficiency of 88.7%, defined as the percentage of forwarding decisions that successfully produce near-optimal routing paths without requiring fallback assistance, representing a 30% improvement over the shortest-path baseline. These results indicate that reinforcement learning is a viable foundation for autonomous, latency-aware routing in dynamically reconfiguring satellite networks.

Abstract: Human-AI collaboration requires recursive epistemic reasoning capabilities that enable artificial agents to explicitly model higher-order mental states, including mutual beliefs regarding knowledge and uncertainty. This paper presents Recursive Mutual Epistemic Networks (RMEN), a neuro-symbolic architecture capable of third-order Theory of Mind reasoning through nested Kripke structures with gradient-based accessibility relations. Ablation studies verify that recursive depth significantly outperforms firstorder approximations, and sensitivity analysis confirms robustness under linguistic uncertainty. These results establish theoretical foundations for transparent human-AI collaboration through explicit, inspectable mental state modeling, though validation with human subjects remains necessary to assess performance under behavioral noise and non-stationary dynamics.

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex reasoning tasks. Existing studies mainly enhance the complex reasoning ability of LLMs through chain-of-thought reasoning, tool augmentation, experience knowledge reuse, and multi-agent collaboration. However, existing methods still suffer from clear limitations in adaptive scheduling for tasks of different difficulty levels and in the organization of collaborative reasoning. Most frameworks apply a uniform heavyweight reasoning pipeline to all problems, lack a dynamic path selection mechanism based on task complexity, and often organize multi-agent collaboration as parallel answer generation followed by competition or voting, which is not well suited to complex reasoning tasks with strong step dependencies. To address these issues, we propose AdaSolve, an adaptive episodic-knowledge-enhanced multi-agent reasoning framework. AdaSolve builds an adaptive routing mechanism based on a complexity classifier: simple problems are solved through direct reasoning, whereas complex problems activate an enhanced path. For complex problems, the framework further introduces experience knowledge retrieval and model self-recall mechanisms to provide historical reasoning experience as references for the current problem. Then, a planning agent decomposes the problem into ordered subtasks, and multiple agents cooperate in a serial manner to perform subtask reasoning, result synthesis, and answer verification. In this way, AdaSolve improves the stability and interpretability of complex problem solving. Experiments on GSM8K, MATH-500, and AIME show that AdaSolve achieves substantial and consistent performance gains over the base model across difficulty levels, and remains competitive with strong experience-enhanced baselines. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of complexity classification and serial multi-agent collaboration. Token-consumption analysis also shows that the method improves reasoning performance while maintaining system efficiency, demonstrating the advantage of combining adaptive episodic knowledge enhancement with serial multi-agent reasoning for complex reasoning tasks.

Abstract: Timed automata learned from fault-free operation data are an established tool for anomaly detection in Cyber-Physical Production Systems, but they provide no mechanism for fault diagnosis: the automaton operates at the signal level and encodes neither the physical meaning of its states nor the causal relationships needed to reason from an observed anomaly to its root cause. We address this by constructing a semantically enriched knowledge graph that supplies the missing context, integrating the learned automaton with the physical plant model represented in AutomationML. Thus, we ground its states and detected anomalies in the physical process they represent. Building on this knowledge graph, a two-stage large language model agent pipeline generates natural-language state descriptions and diagnoses root causes of detected anomaly syndromes without task-specific training data, fault signature libraries, or manually crafted rules. Evaluated on a simulated modular production system benchmark across ten configurations of increasing complexity, state descriptions achieve near-perfect accuracy (99.5% on states observed in fault-free operation, 100% on anomaly-induced states). Syndrome diagnosis identified the correct root cause in 99.4% of localized faults. Propagating faults, whose effects span multiple states, remain the harder case at 76.5%. The results demonstrate that semantic grounding of learned behavioral models is a viable path toward adaptive fault diagnosis where neither fault history nor expert annotations are available.

Abstract: With the widespread application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in smart city scenarios under the Internet of Everything, multi-UAV collaborative trajectory planning faces multiple challenges including cost constraints, collision risks, and complex action spaces. Abstract: Path planning is a fundamental task in robotics, autonomous systems, and spatial optimization, in which real-time and energy-efficient computations are crucial. Conventional digital architectures exhibit limited parallelism when exploring large search spaces, leading to challenges in power efficiency, latency, and scalability. The Ising model offers a promising hardware framework for addressing such problems through energy-minimization dynamics. The spins that represent obstacles and paths in an Ising model update simultaneously, providing substantial acceleration in large-scale pathfinding. However, existing implementations are constrained by inefficient problem mapping and are typically limited to two-dimensional (2D) scenarios. To address these challenges, this work presents a CMOS Ising machine with a three-dimensional (3D) lattice topology for efficient 3D path planning, achieving a 91.3% reduction in transistor count compared with prior work. CMOS simulations verify that the proposed system correctly solves a 16 × 16 × 16 maze within 45 iterations, consuming 8.625 μW per spin and occupying 496.31 μm2 per spin.

Abstract: Mars aerial exploration is a core direction of deep space exploration, and the attitude control of quadrotor aircraft is the key technology to ensure its flight stability. However, the Martian environment with thin atmospheric density and frequent dust storms poses extremely high requirements for the stability and adaptive anti-disturbance capability of the control method for rotor robots. Traditional control methods such as Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) and Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) rely on accurate dynamic models and have poor adaptive capacity to unknown disturbances; pure Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) methods represented by Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) suffer from weak training efficiency and unstable random exploration in the early stage. For the trajectory tracking control method of underactuated quadrotor UAV, the coordinated position attitude coupling compensation is mainly studied. It improves the tracking accuracy under nominal conditions, but heavily depends on accurate dynamic modeling and assuming bounded interference. A fast nonsingular terminal sliding mode combined with angular velocity planning(FNTSM-AVP) is used for the full attitude control of quadrotor. It has finite time convergence and strong interference suppression ability in the earth environment. However, its performance depends on accurate parameter tuning and system dynamics knowledge. In contrast, PG-DDPG optimizes its control strategy online through reinforcement learning, thus maintaining stable control performance even when the model is imprecise. PG-DDPG can also gradually adapt to unknown disturbances through empirical learning and strategy optimization. Existing hybrid control methods combining PID and DRL mostly adopt fixed weight fusion and lack a smooth control authority transfer mechanism, which cannot well adapt to the harsh Martian flight environment. To address these problems, this study proposes a PID-Guided Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (PG-DDPG) hybrid control framework for Mars quadrotor attitude control. Inspired by the natural teaching behavior of gradual guidance reduction, a dynamic exponential decay weighting mechanism is designed to integrate the stable feedback of PID with the adaptive intelligence of DDPG, realizing a smooth transition of control authority from PID-dominated to DRL-dominated during training. First, a six-degree-of-freedom nonlinear dynamic model of Mars quadrotor is established with consideration of Martian gravity and motor dynamic response, and then the state-action space and a multi-component composite reward function are designed for the attitude control task. Finally, the framework is validated through both extensive simulation experiments and hardware implementation on a real quadrotor platform under simulated Martian disturbance conditions. Extensive simulation experiments and physical platform validation show that the rise time of PG-DDPG is 79% faster than PID, 37.5% faster than ADRC, and 21% faster than standard DDPG. The settling time of PG-DDPG is 46.8% less than PID, 35.9% less than ADRC, and 16.7% less than standard DDPG. For continuous disturbances, maximum attitude deviation was reduced by 82.4% compared to PID, 49.5% compared to ADRC, and 14.9% compared to standard DDPG, while recovery times improved by 95.8%, 75.7%, and 33.3% respectively. For transient impact disturbances, despite slightly higher peak overshoot, PG-DDPG achieved significantly faster recovery times (82.5% faster than PID, 34.3% faster than ADRC, and 12% faster than DDPG). The PG-DDPG approach demonstrated approximately 30% greater training efficiency compared to standard DDPG. The proposed framework provides a robust solution for Mars quadrotor attitude control and also offers a new idea for the fusion of classical control and deep reinforcement learning in complex aerospace control scenarios.

Abstract: Digital twin technology offers the feasibility of real-time control of production processes, significantly improving equipment health management, production process optimization, and resource scheduling efficiency. However, current production control still relies on manual experience-based decision-making, which is limited by response lag, strong subjectivity, and poor adaptability, making it difficult to cope with the multi-objective conflicts and dynamic disturbances in complex manufacturing environments. This research aims to overcome the bottlenecks of traditional experience-based control by constructing a digital twin control architecture driven by multi-agent collaboration, thereby upgrading the control mode from passive loss prevention to proactive intervention. This architecture comprises a physical perception layer, a digital twin interaction layer, and a multi-agent collaborative decision-making layer. The method agent is responsible for real-time response to disturbance events such as equipment failures and emergency orders, generating prioritized control plans based on case-based reasoning. The mechanism agent optimizes the system's anti-interference rules through deep reinforcement learning, enhancing system resilience. The resource agent strategically restructures production factors, forming a three-level adaptive closed loop consisting of instantaneous disturbance event response, short-term anti-interference rule iteration, and long-term resource reorganization. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed architecture is demonstrated by a case study of a conveyor jam.

Abstract: The fast development of the swarm robotics has brought new prospects of large-scale autonomous exploration in the complex and uncertain contexts. Abstract: This paper presents SHARP (Supercomputing for High-speed Avoidance and Reactive Planning), a proof-of-concept study demonstrating how high-performance computing (HPC) can enable millisecond-scale responsiveness in robotic control. By reporting per-stage timing and success rates, this study provides a reproducible template for assessing the real-time feasibility of HPC-driven robotics. Collectively, SHARP reframes HPC offloading as a viable pathway toward dependable, reactive robots in dynamic environments.

Abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid optimization–learning framework that integrates the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) with Reinforcement Learning (RL) to accelerate nonlinear model predictive control (MPC) in real time. By leaving the underlying formulation and ADMM update equations unchanged, the proposed RL-enhanced scheme preserves the solution structure of the original optimization problem while significantly reducing the number of iterations required for convergence. Extensive simulations, including Monte Carlo analyses over randomized operating points, demonstrate improved computational efficiency with closed-loop performance comparable to standard ADMM-based MPC. Experimental results on the physical plant further highlight the effectiveness of RL-based meta-optimization as a practical strategy for real-time control of complex nonlinear systems. Note to Practitioners—In real-time industrial applications, the main limitation of model predictive control is often not the control design itself, but the computational effort required to solve the optimization problem at each sampling step. When computational resources are limited or fast sampling rates are required, this can lead to degraded performance or even infeasibility in practice. The proposed approach can be used to reduce the computational burden of existing ADMM-based MPC implementations without modifying the control formulation. By automatically improving the initialization of the solver and tuning its internal parameters online, the method reduces the number of iterations required to reach convergence, especially during transients or disturbances. From a practical perspective, the method is easy to integrate, as it operates as an external module and does not require changes to the system model, constraints, or control objectives. It is particularly useful in applications where similar optimization problems are solved repeatedly over time (e.g., process control, energy systems, or multi-agent coordination), and where reducing computation time directly translates into faster sampling, lower hardware requirements, or improved responsiveness.

Abstract: The deep integration of computing power and electric power systems offers a promising solution to address the escalating energy demands of digital infrastructure and the intermittency of renewable energy. However, realizing efficient synergy confronts temporal heterogeneity between the relatively slow physical dynamics of power systems and the real-time computing demands, compounded by dual uncertainties in renewable generation and computing tasks. To mitigate these challenges, we establish a Digital Twin (DT)-driven hierarchical architecture that leverages high-fidelity virtual mappings to capture, analyze, and predict the dynamics of computing power and electric power systems. Within this architecture, we design a dual time-scale interaction mechanism that coordinates large time-scale energy planning to guide small time-scale adaptive task scheduling. To optimize system performance, we formulate an optimization problem that maximizes carbon emission efficiency, which jointly captures the tradeoff among computational throughput, latency, and carbon emissions under Quality of Service (QoS) constraints. To solve this problem, we propose a Prediction-Augmented Dual Time-Scale Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (PD-MAPPO) algorithm. Simulation results based on real-world meteorological datasets show that PD-MAPPO reduces carbon emissions by 4.6% and average service latency by 3.3% compared with the best-performing baseline in large-scale deployments, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness in synergistic computing power and electric power systems.

Abstract: Robotic contact-rich and fine-grained manipulation remains a significant challenge due to complex interaction dynamics and the competing requirements of multi-timescale control. Simultaneously, the Micro-Residual Corrector (MRC) uses TCP wrench feedback sampled at 60 Hz and a lightweight GRU to provide residual action compensation. Abstract: Automated process planning in variant-rich manufacturing requires the discovery of suitable resource capabilities in heterogeneous production environments. Existing approaches rely either on rigid vocabulary matching with limited flexibility, or on AI-driven methods lacking transparency and real-time applicability. This paper proposes a multi-stage capability discovery architecture that balances matching precision against computational cost through explicit escalation logic. The three stages of the process are applied sequentially, and each stage is invoked only if the preceding stages fail to produce sufficient results. They are as follows: a deterministic ECLASS-based lookup within Asset Administration Shell (AAS) submodels, knowledge-graph reasoning via DIN 8580 taxonomy traversal, and sentence-embedding similarity search. Escalation is governed by match confidence, result completeness, and infrastructure availability. The validation of discovered capabilities is achieved through property constraint checking. The architecture is evaluated on robotic deburring scenarios under varying requirement specificity. On a 69-capability deburring testbed, the full pipeline achieves P@1 = 0.875 and MRR = 0.910 on 88 previously unseen queries, while the staged design keeps median latency below 1 ms for known-vocabulary queries and below 400 ms for the full pipeline on CPU.

Abstract: Robotic navigation in human environments requires not only safety and efficiency but also comfort and social awareness. Abstract: Long-range autonomous rover traverses for future lunar missions, such as the Endurance concept, demand high-fidelity, large-scale testbeds to validate perception and localization systems under extreme polar conditions. Existing testing approaches have a critical trade-off: physical testbeds using lunar simulant may be terramechanically accurate, but are costly, hazardous, and limited in scale, while purely digital simulations can be flexibly modified, but lack the accuracy of real-world terramechanics and sensor readings. We propose a novel hybrid approach, “Replacement Reality” which combines the rigor of physical testing with the flexibility of simulated testing. Replacement Reality integrates a real-time, photorealistic simulation into the perception pipeline of a physical rover. As the hardware traverses terrestrial environments, its onboard camera imagery is replaced with a localized synthetic lunar scene, allowing the autonomy stack to be tested against lunar relevant scenes and simulated hazards like craters and boulders while responding to physical dynamics. The system has been developed and tested on pre-scanned terrains on the order of tens of meters in length and width (with plans to extend that to kilometers). The pre-scanned terrains have been augmented with craters and the rover is localized within these areas using onboard visual inertial odometry and a iterative closest point algorithm to achieve centimeter-level accuracy. Augmented rocks and craters were either small not to impact the mobility or non-traversable to prevent traversability mismatches between simulation and reality. Publication Title: 2026 IEEE/ASME International Conference on Advanced Intelligent Mechatronics (AIM)
Abstract: This paper presents the integrated design of SPARC (Smart Platooning Autonomous Robot Chair), a low-cost, lightweight smart wheelchair developed to enhance mobility for people with disabilities in indoor environments such as hospitals, airports, and assisted-care facilities. The proposed system addresses key limitations of existing smart wheelchairs—including high cost, excessive weight, limited modularity, and sensor over-specification—through a carefully optimized sensor suite tailored for indoor navigation requirements. SPARC integrates an embedded PC with ROS2 (Robot Operating System), four lightweight Tmini-Pro 2D LiDARs distributed to provide 360-degree environmental coverage, a RealSense D435i RGB-D camera mounted above the user for visual tracking applications, and a Pixhawk 2.4.8 IMU positioned near the center of gravity for accurate orientation and acceleration measurements. Experimental validation demonstrates the effectiveness of this sensor configuration through a visual servoing application involving a fleet of three wheelchairs tracking AprilTags. Results confirm that the distributed sensor architecture successfully captures dynamic multi-agent interactions by measuring other physical parameters using encoders, LiDARs, and IMUs. Those lightweight, optimally placed sensors can deliver performance comparable to heavier, more expensive alternatives. SPARC’s modular, cost-effective design could support other smart functionalities in the future, such as obstacle avoidance, cooperative control, and AI-driven path planning.

Abstract: Network Digital Twin (NDT) and network slicing are key technologies for the next-generation mobile networks (6G), enabling a transformation in network planning, construction, and operation. However, existing 5G networks face issues such as heterogeneous resource types, differing management strategies among operators, and cross-domain data privacy constraints, which hinder the interoperability of node resources and state information. This paper proposes the use of a DT network to create virtual counterparts of physical nodes, enabling cross-domain information exchange and collaborative optimization across Radio Access Network (RAN) and Core Network (CN) domains. The main contributions are: (1) a DT-based cross-domain heterogeneous network slicing architecture, using Software Defined Network (SDN) to mirror the operating states of physical nodes for interaction and collaboration between slices and twins; (2) a physical network model for pretraining resource scheduling strategies at the physical network layer; (3) a transfer learning mechanism to migrate pretrained strategy parameters from the physical to the virtual twin network, establishing collaborative resource allocation between the twin and physical networks. This mechanism further supports coordination between AI-RAN and the CN. Simulation results show that the proposed solution outperforms the baseline in multi-agent resource scheduling tasks, demonstrating significant improvements in cross-domain collaboration and joint resource scheduling in a multi-slice heterogeneous environment.

Abstract: The widespread adoption of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has made the safe and efficient coordination of multi-UAV systems in complex environments a critical research challenge. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an adaptive cooperative trajectory planning method for multi-UAV systems through an enhanced deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework: First, we innovatively integrate a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network and incorporates a burn-in mechanism into the environment perception module of the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm. Third, we adopt a cross-agent shared-parameter architecture to accelerate the model development process for multi-UAV systems, thereby formulating efficient autonomous navigation strategies for UAVs. Experimental results demonstrate that compared to both relatively advanced DRL approaches and traditional approaches, the proposed algorithm exhibits significant advantages in convergence, stability, and effectiveness.

Abstract: Background: Adaptive gait trajectory prediction is essential to achieve natural and stable locomotion in prosthetic limbs and legged robots, particularly under varied conditions such as changing inclines and walking speeds. Methods: This study proposes a Bayesian deep neural network framework for predicting continuous joint trajectories in the sagittal plane across diverse ambulation tasks. The approach integrates Bayesian inference to estimate predictive uncertainty and enhance model generalization. A new hybrid loss function is introduced that combines the standard error of the dataset with variational mean absolute error or mean squared error, allowing the model to leverage low-variance gait segments more effectively during training. The framework is trained and evaluated using a dataset that includes varying walking speeds and inclines. Moreover, the Bayesian deep neural network provides 95% prediction intervals, indicating strong reliability and robustness under uncertain conditions. Significance: By incorporating uncertainty quantification and dataset-driven variance into the learning process, this study offers a more reliable and adaptive approach to gait modeling. These improvements support enhanced gait control in assistive technologies and legged robotic systems operating in variable terrain conditions in the real world.

Authors: Amarjeet; O. Surtani; P. Sahoo
Author Affiliations: Department of Mathematics, Birla Institute of Technology, Ranchi, India; Department of Mathematics, Birla Institute of Technology, Ranchi, India; Department of Electronics and Instrumentation Engineering, National Institute of Technology, Rourkela, Odisha, India
Publication Title: 2026 IEEE 1st International Conference on Instrumentation (INSTCon)
Abstract: The Green-on-Green problem — distinguishing crop seedlings from weeds during early post-emergence growth — remains a stubborn perception challenge in agricultural robotics. Standard RGB cameras collapse the biochemical differences between co-occurring plant species into three broad colour channels, leaving deep learning models to rely on textures and shapes that are often indistinguishable at the seedling stage. Hyperspectral imaging resolves this ambiguity by sampling narrow spectral bands across the visible range, but hardware sensors costing upwards of $5,000 remain impractical for smallholder farms and low-cost robotic platforms.We present a two-stage cascade pipeline that addresses this cost barrier through deep spectral reconstruction. An MST++ spectral transformer first reconstructs a 31-band visible hyperspectral cube (400–700 nm) from a single RGB image, achieving PSNR = 45.41 dB and SSIM = 0.9975 on the NTIRE 2022 ARAD-1K benchmark in under sixteen minutes of training. The reconstructed bands are then fused with the original RGB image inside our proposed Dual-Encoder Fusion Network (DEFNet), which processes the two modalities through independent encoder streams and a learnable SpectralAttention mechanism — preventing the dominant RGB signal from suppressing weaker spectral features, a failure mode we identified and corrected during development. Segmentation experiments on the 400-image Peanut Weed Dataset yield an mIoU of 82.64%, against 81.07% for a rigorously matched RGB-only baseline and 79.54% reported by the dataset’s original authors on the same benchmark. Because both models share identical architecture scale, training schedule, and data split, the +1.93% absolute gain directly isolates the contribution of reconstructed spectral information. Qualitative analysis confirms that improvements concentrate at weed boundaries and small isolated seedlings — where spectral cues carry the most discriminatory value. Code and a reproducible Colab notebook are released publicly.

Abstract: Achieving energy-efficient and load-independent actuation remains a major challenge in robotic and mechanical systems, especially in dynamic environments where payload variation and unpredictable loading can significantly affect performance. The research paper presents a new self-balancing kinematic automation system whereby compliance is enforced with symmetry, neural energy surface learning, and friction-based passive holding are introduced in order to achieve consistent motion with varying loads. It has the screw-theoretic constraint modeling, force polytope optimization, and combinatorial topology design system architecture to generate high-fidelity actuation planning. Torque shaping controller with passive friction constraints can provide adaptive control with reasonable use of energy. The model has been tested in a series of tasks of variable weights, load change and inclination still holding. The experimental findings show that the actuation accuracy is 95.67 on average, and the energy savings are more than $40 \%$ of that of rigid actuator systems. It had successful passivity holding $94-100 \%$ to a level of 45 degrees with regard to the tilt which demonstrated high stability in the gravity affected conditions. This structure is especially applicable in energy-intensive systems like autonomous robots, industrial arms and prosthetic devices. The combination of predictive control and self-balancing physical structures can provide a route to strong, intelligent and sustainable next-generation automation of mechanical systems.

Abstract: We present a novel method for the automatic real-time analysis and semantic modeling of pedestrian zones, designed to enhance spatial orientation and autonomous navigation systems in complex urban environments. The proposed approach integrates an optimized image processing pipeline comprising three key stages: semantic segmentation using a modified U-Net convolutional neural network, iterative post-processing for noise reduction and boundary refinement, and the generation of semantic embeddings for key scene points.The modified U-Net architecture incorporates encoder-decoder pathways with skip connections, batch normalization, and dropout regularization, enabling precise pixel-level classification of critical scene elements such as sidewalks, crosswalks, obstacles, and other navigable zones. Post-processing combines Gaussian and median filtering with edge detection and Hough Transform-based line extraction to produce smooth, continuous pedestrian-area boundaries. A distinguishing feature of this method is the generation of high-dimensional semantic embeddings for intersection points and other key features. These embeddings allow for the establishment of robust correspondences between different views, enabling accurate 3D reconstruction, alignment of multiple images, and the creation of semantically enriched spatial maps. Performance evaluation demonstrates that the approach maintains high accuracy and efficiency under dynamic urban conditions, including varying illumination and dense pedestrian traffic. The proposed framework provides a comprehensive solution for real-time autonomous navigation, robotic path planning, and augmented reality applications, combining both geometric and semantic understanding of pedestrian spaces. Its modular design facilitates integration into existing navigation pipelines and represents a significant step toward fully intelligent urban mobility systems.

Abstract: Generative world models facilitate robotic planning through future prediction, but existing navigation models (NWM) lack 3D geometric grounding, failing in complex 6DoF humanoid environments. We present Geo-NWM (GeometricNavigation World Model), a framework integrating conditional diffusion transformers with sparse visual SLAM priors to enforce geometric consistency. A consistency loss formalized on the SE(3) manifold penalizes physics-violating pixel motions, stabilizing diffusion gradients and mitigating trajectory hallucinations. The dual-stream architecture fuses a SLAM geometric anchor with a generative diffusion dreamer via a Geometric Gate layer. We introduce the Dream-to-Reality ATE (D-ATE) metric to quantify physical fidelity. Validation on the Unitree G1 in MuJoCo demonstrates an 80% reduction in trajectory drift, providing a robust foundation for safe human-robot interaction in shared environments.
